source_facts: CairnClass 8.0 is a synthetic district roster service. This specification is authoritative for moving one district's class roster from CSV format 2 to format 3. The audience is district data managers, not classroom teachers. The supported district in the example is pine-district. The exact protected paragraph is: 'Grade exports: Grade-export files continue to use their existing layout. This roster transition does not change grade-export delivery.' It must remain verbatim. The update scope is roster format compatibility, cutover, and recovery; it does not include grade-export changes. In format 2 the column named room stores a human-readable room label. In format 3 the replacement column is room_code and stores a stable facilities-directory identifier. This is not a cosmetic header rename: the values require a mapping. The room map for this transition maps Cedar Hall to CH-12. Blank room labels map to the literal UNASSIGNED. An unknown nonblank room label blocks conversion; it must not be silently mapped to UNASSIGNED. Other roster columns are carried through unchanged. The approved room map must exist before conversion. A dated copy of the original format-2 roster must be archived before conversion. The example original is roster-v2.csv, the approved mapping is rooms.csv, the archive is archive/roster-v2-2026-09-14.csv, and the converted output is roster-v3.csv. District managers use the existing archive process rather than a new shell-copy instruction on this page. Run `cairn roster convert --input roster-v2.csv --room-map rooms.csv --output roster-v3.csv`; conversion writes a new file and does not activate a district roster. The service must have automated roster imports paused before activation. Run `cairn roster activate --district pine-district --file roster-v3.csv` to activate the converted roster. Activation is atomic: the whole converted roster becomes active or the prior roster remains active on failure. A successful activation returns a revision identifier that the data manager records in the district change ticket. In format-3 operation, the service rejects format-2 roster uploads; the bulletin must not promise an overlap period. Automated imports resume only after their producer emits format 3. The producer adjustment is performed through its existing maintenance process; no producer command is specified here. Before the first successful format-3 activation, recovery can use the archived format-2 file through the existing format-2 import process. After that activation, the archive cannot be directly re-uploaded as a rollback; contact District Data Operations for recovery. The archive remains useful as evidence of the original labels after the direct-reupload boundary closes. `roster-format-3.md` is the supplemental format reference and `district-archives.md` is the existing archive-process reference. All necessary compatibility rules, transformation meanings, commands, prerequisites, and recovery boundaries are supplied here.

# CairnClass roster format 3 transition

District data managers use this bulletin for the pine-district roster cutover in CairnClass 8.0. The transition concerns class roster files. Keep the district change ticket with the roster work so the resulting revision can be connected to the prepared source file.

## Activate the converted roster

Run `cairn roster activate --district pine-district --file roster-v3.csv`. Activation is atomic: the whole converted roster becomes active, or a failure leaves the prior roster active. Record the returned revision identifier in the district change ticket after success.

## One transformed room

The approved example mapping turns Cedar Hall into CH-12. A blank room label becomes the literal `UNASSIGNED`. An unknown nonblank label blocks conversion instead of being silently assigned that literal. District managers should use the approved map rather than infer a code from how a room name is abbreviated in another document.

## Grade exports

Grade exports: Grade-export files continue to use their existing layout. This roster transition does not change grade-export delivery.

## Recovery boundary

Before the first successful format-3 activation, the archived format-2 file can be used through the existing format-2 import process. After that activation, it cannot be directly re-uploaded as a rollback. Contact District Data Operations for recovery at that point. The archive still provides evidence of the original room labels even when direct re-upload is no longer an available recovery route.

## Convert a roster

Run `cairn roster convert --input roster-v2.csv --room-map rooms.csv --output roster-v3.csv`. Conversion writes a new file; it does not activate the district roster. Other roster columns are carried through unchanged. The converted file is the input to the activation command above.

## Column background

Format 2 uses `room` for a human-readable room label. Format 3 replaces it with `room_code`, which contains a stable identifier from the facilities directory. The transition therefore changes the meaning of the values as well as the column name. Simply changing the header does not convert a file. [Roster format 3](roster-format-3.md) is the supplemental format reference.

## Before conversion

An approved room map must exist before conversion. For this example it is `rooms.csv`. Archive a dated copy of the original format-2 roster before conversion as well; the example archive is `archive/roster-v2-2026-09-14.csv`. Use the existing [District archives](district-archives.md) process rather than inventing a separate archive procedure for this bulletin.

## File acceptance

Once the district operates in format 3, the service rejects format-2 roster uploads. There is no period in which managers can assume either format will work. That compatibility boundary also explains why keeping an archive is not the same as having an unlimited direct-upload rollback option.

## Import scheduling

Automated roster imports must be paused before activation. Resume them only after their producer emits format 3. Use the producer's existing maintenance process for that adjustment; this bulletin does not supply a producer command. These scheduling conditions apply to the cutover even though conversion itself only creates a local file.
